text:
Travis Sanheim plays almost 25 minutes a night for Philadelphia, and he has made them count lately: 3 goals in his last ten games, including the tying goal late in Edmonton on Nov. 11 and another against Buffalo on Nov. 17.

At 30, he is the Flyers' most reliable defenseman. Evolving-Hockey ranked him 23rd among 215 defensemen last season, with value coming from both ends, against competition in the 92nd percentile. He has 4 goals and 6 assists in 25 games, and 51 blocked shots.

The goals are real, not a hot streak. His 4 goals match the 4.07 expected goals on his own shots almost exactly. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking explains where they come from: he gets to the home-plate area in front of the net more than most defensemen (86th percentile), and 33% of his shots came off the rush last season, about double the typical defenseman.

What hasn't been kind is the team around him. Philadelphia has scored 3.4 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him points. That usually evens out.
headline: Carrying the minutes
